prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and proposals

Economy, tax and welfare
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027 and abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by the end of the Parliament. No rises in the main rates of income tax or VAT.
- Introduce “Triple Lock Plus” so the State Pension and a new age‑related personal allowance for pensioners rise by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%. Maintain pensioner benefits and no new taxes on pensions.
- Expand 30 hours’ free childcare from nine months to school start by Sept 2025; move Child Benefit to a household test with taper between £120k–£160k.
- Reform welfare: tighten work capability assessments, overhaul fit notes, expand mental health support, tougher sanctions for long‑term unemployment, accelerate Universal Credit rollout, and strengthen anti‑fraud powers.

Business, growth and infrastructure
- Maintain full expensing and consider extending to leasing; no rise in corporation tax; 10‑point SME plan (rates relief, VAT threshold review, prompt payment, access to finance, regulation cuts).
- Invest HS2 savings (£36bn) in regional roads, rail and buses; nationwide gigabit by 2030 and widespread standalone 5G; speed major infrastructure approvals to one year.
- Raise public R&D to £22bn/year, expand AI, compute and advanced manufacturing; strengthen the City’s competitiveness.

Education, skills and youth
- Protect real‑terms per‑pupil schools funding; recruit and retain teachers; statutory mobile‑phone bans in schools; two hours of PE weekly.
- Introduce the Advanced British Standard for 16–19, keep maths and English to 18, and expand academy trusts and special needs places.
- Create 100,000 additional apprenticeships annually by closing low‑outcome university courses.
- Establish compulsory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military placements or part‑time civic service).

Health and social care
- Increase NHS spending above inflation annually; train 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors; expand Pharmacy First, build/modernise 250 GP surgeries and 50 Community Diagnostic Centres.
- Dental Recovery Plan with more NHS appointments and service obligations for new dentists.
- Invest £3.4bn in NHS tech (NHS App, AI, scans), reduce managers, and implement Major Conditions and Women’s Health strategies; legislate on tobacco and vapes; implement Cass Review guidance.

Housing and communities
- Build 1.6m homes; fast‑track brownfield development; mitigate nutrient rules via developer fees; densify cities; regenerate major sites; maintain Green Belt protections.
- Make permanent first‑time buyer Stamp Duty relief up to £425k; launch a new Help to Buy; Renters Reform Bill to abolish Section 21 alongside court reforms; complete leasehold reform; CGT relief for landlords selling to sitting tenants.
- Recruit 8,000 more neighbourhood police; expand hotspot policing and community payback; tougher sentencing for serious offenders; build four new prisons.

Energy, climate and environment
- Annual oil and gas licensing; maintain windfall tax to 2028–29 (subject to prices); build new gas power stations as backup.
- Treble offshore wind capacity; deliver carbon capture clusters; approve two Small Modular Reactor fleets within 100 days; new plant at Wylfa; speed nuclear approvals.
- Keep the energy price cap; review standing charges; expand smart tariffs; fund £6bn for home energy efficiency plus a universal voucher scheme; support onshore wind with local consent; support rooftop/brownfield solar; retain fracking moratorium.
- Tighten water regulation (bonus bans after serious breaches, unlimited fines), fund river restoration, reform water price reviews; expand tree and peatland schemes; designate a new National Park; tougher fly‑tipping penalties; develop a Deposit Return Scheme; prevent new waste incinerators.

Migration, borders and defence
- Legal annual cap on migration with a yearly parliamentary vote; higher salary thresholds; health checks and higher surcharges; increase visa fees.
- Implement removals to Rwanda; reform asylum rules and pursue international treaty changes; expand returns deals.
- Increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; invest at least £10bn in munitions; raise defence R&D to 5% of the defence budget plus 2% for exploitation; comprehensive veterans package.

Other measures
- Clarify in law that “sex” in the Equality Act means biological sex; update NHS Constitution on single‑sex care.
- Back farming with a £1bn UK‑wide budget increase, a legal food security target, faster farm infrastructure planning, and a successor £100m Seafood Fund.
- Extend the £2 bus fare cap across the Parliament; introduce a Backing Drivers Bill (no road pricing, local votes on new 20mph/Low Traffic schemes).
- Maintain First Past the Post, voter ID, and six‑day Royal Mail service.
